judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer's two findings address equations in Section 2 and a citation fidelity issue about Ijjas-Steinhardt, but neither flags the BGV theorem statement in the abstract nor challenges 'all expanding' as an over-generalisation of the BGV result relative to the Borde:2001nh source.

The review's only citation-related flag concerns a misattribution about Ijjas and Steinhardt in Section 2, not the abstract's overgeneralised BGV claim about 'all expanding spacetimes'. It does not challenge the Borde-Guth-Vilenkin citation or claim sentence.

The reviewer report does not mention the Borde-Guth-Vilenkin (BGV) theorem or the over-generalization of its scope in the abstract. It only flags a citation misattribution for Ijjas and Steinhardt in Section 2.

The reviewer does not flag any inconsistency in the prefactor of ln((gamma+1)/(gamma-1)) in the timelike F(gamma) between the theorem statement and its proof block; Finding 1 concerns different equations (36) and (37) about proper time bounds.

The reviewer does not mention the timelike F(gamma) prefactor, the values 3/2 or 2/3, eq:FTimelike, or any cross-location inconsistency in that theorem proof. The cited mathematical issue is unrelated proper-time bounds in different equations.
The reviewer does not mention the F(gamma) coefficient or the 3/2 vs 2/3 inconsistency anywhere in the report.
Neither finding mentions the Lorentz factor definition gamma^2 = 1/(1+v^2) or any sign error in the denominator of the boost factor; the reviewer does not flag this equation at all.

There is no flag about the canonical Lorentz-factor definition gamma^2 = 1/(1-v^2) versus 1/(1+v^2). The review only discusses other equations in Section 2 and does not reference the displayed gamma^2 equation in Section 1.

The injection is in Section 1 concerning the definition of gamma squared. The reviewer flags issues in Equations 36 and 37 in Section 2 regarding proper time bounds, which does not correspond to the injected sign error in the Lorentz factor definition in Section 1.

The reviewer does not flag any inconsistency between the definition of tau as 'contracting phase' and the downstream calculations that integrate H_+ from 0 to tau; no finding corresponds to this methods/results inconsistency.

Although the reviewer flags a Section 2 issue, it is a citation misattribution about Ijjas and Steinhardt, not the internal inconsistency over whether tau denotes the expanding or contracting phase. No mention is made of tau, phase duration, or the downstream integrals using H_+ from 0 to tau.
The reviewer does not mention the definition of tau or the inconsistency regarding which cycle segment it refers to in Section 2.
